subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: What proof is sufficient before this high-impact fresh-session billing issue can close?
rationale: Source inspection shows the likely guardrails are in place, but the remaining decision is whether maintainers require a focused current-main runtime/provider proof or an additional guardrail before treating the billing path as fixed.

options.title: Prove Current Main Then Close
options.body: Run the exact fresh-session scenario with large trajectory sidecars and close only if the captured context/provider payload proves trajectory bytes are absent.

options.title: Add Runtime Guardrail First
options.body: Keep this open for a defensive test or runtime assertion that fails if trajectory sidecars become model context again.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Artifacts
options.body: Ask the reporter for current-main Windows artifacts before spending maintainer proof time, accepting that the stale issue remains unresolved longer.

recommendation.title: Prove Current Main Then Close
recommendation.body: Run the exact fresh-session scenario with large trajectory sidecars and close only if the captured context/provider payload proves trajectory bytes are absent.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current guardrail is the trajectory artifact classifier added in steipete's trajectory sidecar cleanup work.
